messages:
maria_support: ACME prod report — p99 for streaming initial chunk jumped from ~220ms to ~1.3s after the 2026-03-10 runtime/edge deploy. Customer hitting intermittent timeouts (30s). Sharing repro and quick logs.

maria_support: Repro (from our VPN):
```
curl -N -H "Authorization: Bearer <key>" -H "Accept: text/event-stream" \\
  https://api.redwood.ai/v1/stream?model=gpt-large \\
  -d '{"prompt":"hello world","max_tokens":200}'
```

maria_support: Observed SSE first event arrives ~1.3s. Hitting p99 regression only for streaming; non-stream endpoint for same prompt returns full response in ~800ms.

laura_cs: adding customer detail — they use node-fetch (v3) and see same regression from EU region. Says issue started after that Friday change.

jake_runtime: @maria_support can you paste request id / trace-id and attach the host kernel tag? Also which runtime image? Need to correlate with kernel selection telemetry.

maria_support: trace id: trace-rcpt-00321; runtime image: rwinf/runtime:v2.14.1; route: /v1/stream (stream handler v2). Minimal log line:
```
[2026-03-11T08:12:01Z] request_id=trace-rcpt-00321 handler=streaming queue_ms=3 exec_ms=18 backend_write_ms=1200 proxy_flush_wait_ms=400
```

priya_sre: proxy_flush_wait=400ms is the smoking gun — suggests edge coalescing or gateway buffering. Did we change response coalescing in edge config on 2026-03-10?

ken_platform: yes — we merged an experimental auto-coalesce change (was fixed 200ms -> auto heuristics). We scoped it to canary but a config propagation bug hit more tenants.

jake_runtime: i reproduced locally by toggling edge coalesce to 0 vs 200ms. With coalesce=0 initial chunk ~180ms, with 200ms it matches ~1.2s. Non-stream path unaffected because backend flushes full payload.

maria_support: Repro checklist for SRE/Platform to validate customer repro:
- run the curl -N call above from our testnet
- tcpdump on ingress (filter by request_id)
- enable trace logging for request_id in runtime (trace level on streaming handler)
- toggle tenant-level response_coalesce_ms and re-run

priya_sre: Mitigations we can offer immediately:
- set tenant-level response_coalesce_ms=50 for acme-tenant (low risk)
- enable runtime heartbeat bytes: runtime emits 1B padding every 100ms until tokens stream (forces flush)
- temporary fallback: route that tenant to non-stream endpoint (will increase total response size but avoids coalesce penalty)

laura_cs: customer prefers not to switch to non-streaming (parsing expectations). They accepted a tenant coalesce tweak if low-risk.

ken_platform: i'll roll a targeted config change to set response_coalesce_ms=50 for acme-tenant and monitor. Not touching global default.

deploy-bot: rollback/config-change job queued: job_id=rb-acme-20260312 window=2026-03-12T02:00Z -> 02:10Z. Will apply only to tenant acme-xxxxx.

jake_runtime: one more note: we also saw a later backend_write_ms regression (~+700ms) on some hosts where kernel selection picked a slower memcpy path for certain quantized layers. i'm opening an INF to track (INF-2026-314). That could explain cases where even backend_write_ms is high.

priya_sre: ops plan (short):
- capture 1h of traces and tcpdump (started)
- reproduce with curl (SSE) and node (h2) to see client differences
- apply tenant coalesce=50 in canary for acme and measure p95/p99 for 30m
- if good, promote change to tenant permanently; if not, rollback and use heartbeat fallback

maria_support: customer reported a visible improvement after the canary coalesce change (preliminary). Monitoring p50/p95/p99 now.

laura_cs: customer says UX improved; we'll keep them in the loop for 24h and will escalate if anything returns.

jake_runtime: created an internal troubleshooting note with sample traces and pprof output. Also hooking kernel telemetry to INF-2026-314.

maria_support: next steps: SRE/Platform to complete canary, runtime team to investigate kernel memcpy path, support to keep customer updated. Sync call 16:00 today.

maria_support: :thumbsup:
